items.finalAnswer: Cells are organized into tissues, tissues into organs, and organs into organ systems.

steps: The epithelial tissue forms the inner lining of the stomach and protects its wall from gastric juices.
It secretes mucus, which protects the stomach lining, and gastric juice, which helps in the digestion of food.
items.finalAnswer: Stomach epithelium protects the stomach wall and secretes mucus and gastric juice.

steps: The smooth muscles in the stomach contract and relax to churn and mix food with gastric juices.
Their contractions also push the partly digested food towards the small intestine.
items.finalAnswer: Smooth muscles churn food with gastric juices and move it towards the small intestine.

steps: Palisade mesophyll cells contain many chloroplasts.
They absorb light and carry out most of the photosynthesis in the leaf.
items.finalAnswer: Palisade mesophyll carries out most of the photosynthesis in the leaf.

steps: The shoot system consists of the stem, leaves, buds, flowers and fruits.
It supports the plant and bears its leaves and reproductive structures.
Leaves make food by photosynthesis, while flowers take part in reproduction.
items.finalAnswer: The shoot system supports the plant, bears its leaves and reproductive structures, and helps in food-making and reproduction.

steps: Homeostasis is the maintenance of a relatively stable internal environment in an organism despite changes in the external environment.
It is important because cells and their enzymes function properly only when internal conditions remain within suitable limits.
items.finalAnswer: Homeostasis keeps an organism’s internal environment stable so its cells and enzymes can function properly.

steps: The hypothalamus in the brain monitors the temperature of the blood and helps regulate body temperature.
When the body is too warm, sweat glands produce sweat and skin blood vessels widen; evaporation of sweat and increased blood flow to the skin help lose heat.
When the body is too cold, skin blood vessels narrow to reduce heat loss, and muscles may shiver to produce heat.
items.finalAnswer: The hypothalamus helps maintain body temperature by coordinating sweating and widening of skin blood vessels when hot, and shivering and narrowing of skin blood vessels when cold.

steps: Tissue: A group of similar cells that work together to perform a particular function.
Organ: A structure made of different tissues working together to perform a particular function.
Example: In the stomach, epithelial, muscular and other tissues work together as an organ.
items.finalAnswer: A tissue is a group of similar cells performing a function, whereas an organ is made of different tissues working together.
